articles.title: Crystal Brains and Mercury Blood: Why Consciousness Might Not Need Biology
articles.summary: A new philosophical paper argues that consciousness could emerge from wildly different materials—like crystal or mercury. With an estimated 1,000+ advanced alien civilizations possibly out there, the universe may host minds stranger than we can imagine.

articles.title: 1.8 Million Years Ago, Early Humans Were Already Bringing Fire Into Caves
articles.summary: New evidence from South Africa's Wonderwerk Cave shows hominins were transporting fire deep inside and maintaining it between 1.07 and 1.79 million years ago. The finding pushes back the timeline of intentional fire use and reveals active engagement, not passive opportunism.

articles.title: A Butterfly That Barely Ages Could Unlock the Secrets of Longevity
articles.summary: Heliconius butterflies live up to 348 days—25 times longer than close relatives—and one species shows almost no physical decline with age. Even without their unique pollen diet, they outlive others, suggesting evolved mechanisms for slow aging that could inform human longevity research.
